text:
maria_devex: Heads-up — customer #C-812 just escalated. Sudden billing spike + increased 401s after we merged the OpenAPI regen from yesterday. They say client retries doubled traffic. Can we triage? :grimacing:

sam_sdk: which client/lang and versions? any repro steps?

maria_devex: They use our hosted API via our TypeScript client (v1.3.0 -> upgraded to v1.4.0 from CI regen). Also a few services still on Python v0.9.8 but main spike came from TS. Support ticket includes logs.

lee_support: paste of snippets from customer logs: 
```
2026-03-12T15:10:02Z INFO request start method=POST path=/v1/generate
2026-03-12T15:10:02Z ERROR response status=401 body="{\"error\":\"Unauthorized\"}"
2026-03-12T15:10:02Z WARN retry attempt=1 reason=401 immediately_retry=true
2026-03-12T15:10:02Z INFO request start method=POST path=/v1/generate
2026-03-12T15:10:02Z INFO response status=200 tokens=124
```
Customer says the TS client started an immediate retry on 401 instead of failing fast. That doubled billable tokens for some requests.

sam_sdk: hmm. Our retry policy should not retry on 401. CI regen change might have messed up the default retry filter. Can you bisect the regen commit?

maria_devex: I ran a quick diff between openapi spec commits and client gen template: the regen added a new `retryOn` config to the generated client and defaulted it to `['5xx','401']` instead of only `['5xx']`. File: clients/ts/templates/retry.ts (added line).

jen_bughunt: confirmed locally. Checkout commit `feat/openapi-regen-20260311` then run: 
```
# repro with minimal script
npm i @redwood/sdk@1.4.0
node -e "const c=require('@redwood/sdk'); c.generate({prompt:'hi'}).catch(e=>console.error(e));"
```
Output shows immediate retry on 401; code reveals generator set `shouldRetry = status === 401 || status >= 500`.

olivia_sre: deploy-bot shows regression in CI: deploy-bot:regen-check reported generated clients diffed but no failing test. We don't have an automated integration test that asserts retry semantics for auth failures.

maria_devex: customer impact notes: spike lasted ~12 minutes while their service retried -> estimated +40% token bill. They've asked for rollback and RCA.

sam_sdk: short fix options: 
- patch generator template to remove 401 from retry list and cut v1.4.1 release (TS + Python regen),
- advise customer to pin to 1.3.0 temporarily,
- add a quick e2e test to CI that asserts `doNotRetryOn(401)` for all SDKs.

lee_support: customer already rolled back to pinned 1.3.0 — we should confirm their bill adjustment request and give recommended mitigation.

jen_bughunt: I'll prepare a patch. Quick change in templates/retry.ts: replace `const RETRY_ON = ['401','5xx']` with `const RETRY_ON = ['5xx']`. Also add a unit for header auth flow.

olivia_sre: for rollout safety, let's also gate regen merges in CI until we have: (1) smoke test for retry behavior (401 not retried) and (2) a changelog entry summarizing any default policy changes.

sam_sdk: add to release checklist: verify regen doesn't introduce new default retry policies or changes to auth header handling. Also check Python/Go clients for parity.

maria_devex: I already asked support to flag billing team. They asked for a formal RCA and timeline for patch release. ETA?

jen_bughunt: patch PR in a few hours. Will coordinate hotfix release for TS client and a regen of other SDKs.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: CI pipeline starting: regen-smoke-tests -> will run unit+retry-e2e on ts/python/go.

olivia_sre: once PR is up, I'll run a canary against staging to confirm no further immediate-retry on 401 and measure request rate.

sam_sdk: follow-up tasks: 
- [ ] PR to fix template + release v1.4.1 (TS) + regen Python/Go clients
- [ ] Pin guidance in Support KB + rollback steps (how to pin: `npm install @redwood/sdk@1.3.0` / `pip install redwood-sdk==0.9.8`)

maria_devex: I'll update the customer with interim mitigation and ETA for patch. Thanks team. :pray:
